Hi Dylan / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Stellar's traffic pattern for the holiday pilot looks stronger than we expected — we ran a spike test and the headroom planning shows we need a higher committed monthly token quota to avoid throttling during peaks.

Quick summary of what Stellar needs:
- Move from our current 3M token/month hosted commit to 7M token/month for the pilot months (Aug–Oct).
- Maintain a burst pocket to 12M tokens/month with prorated overage pricing.
- Lower latency tail guarantee -> target p95 <= 220ms for SeqLen 256.

Can you confirm whether that pricing and the SLA tweak map to a simple amendment (monthly commit + burst add-on + latency annex)? Priya on contracts is CC'ed — she will coordinate internal approvals.

Attaching the traffic projection and the initial PO draft.

Thanks,
Elliott
Head of Integrations, Stellar Retail

Attachments: traffic_projection_q3.csv (csv), initial_po_stellar.pdf (pdf)

Quick feasibility check after looking at model profiles and current cluster utilization:

- Capacity: The 7M/month committed token profile for Aug–Oct maps to an estimated avg throughput of ~2.2k tokens/sec sustained during peak windows. On our current hosted pools, that fits but reduces buffer for other tenants. To keep p95 <= 220ms we need either:
  - a routing preference to higher-priority tiers during peak windows (ops changes), or
  - provision an isolated Dedicated pool in us-west-2 for the pilot (recommended for predictability).

- Cost/ops tradeoff: Dedicated reservation will raise monthly cost ~30% relative to hosted uplift, but gives us SLA headroom and avoids noisy-neighbor variance. If they insist on Hosted, we should add an explicit fallback: we guarantee soft p95 <= 250ms with an escalation path to Dedicated if observed p95 > 250ms for >72 hours.

- Batching/caching: We can recoup ~8-12% token cost by suggesting KV prefill + persistent prefix cache. Marissa, ops runbook should include the cache TTL and warm-up window.

I'll attach a short technical note for Vanessa to surface in the amendment.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: hosted_sizing_note.pdf (pdf)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — monthly commit increase and burst allocation (Proposed amendment)

Hi Elliott / Priya —

Thanks for the projection. Attached is a proposed Amendment v1 and a short SLA Annex that captures the latency targets and the 72-hour fallback escalation. High-level points: 

- Commit: Add 7,000,000 tokens/month committed from 2026-08-01 through 2026-10-31. Prorated billing for partial months included in the amendment.
- Burst: Add burst pocket to 12,000,000 tokens/month; overage will bill at the negotiated overage rate listed in Section 2 of the amendment.
- SLA: We propose an operational SLA: soft p95 <= 250ms (hosted), with an explicit Dedicated escalation if observed p95 > 250ms for a rolling 72-hour window. For customers who require firm p95 <= 220ms, Dedicated reservation is the recommended option (we've included estimated Dedicated pricing in Appendix A).
- Onboarding: Ops runbook and cache-warm steps included as Attachment B; expected lead time for Dedicated provisioning is 10 business days.

Next steps:
1) Priya — please share any contract redlines you have and confirm PO timeline.
2) Elliott — if you sign off on the soft SLA + escalation approach we will: schedule the onboarding kickoff (Ops + CS) and lock the Aug 1 start.
3) Dylan — if Stellar wants a firm 220ms p95 we need a separate Dedicated SOW; please confirm if that is likely.

I've attached: proposed_amendment_redlines.docx, sla_latency_targets.pdf, hosted_commit_schedule_v3.xlsx (showing billing ramp/ramp-proration).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_amendment_redlines.docx (docx), sla_latency_targets.pdf (pdf), hosted_commit_schedule_v3.xlsx (xlsx)
